The problem

Three blind spots that cost you citations

AI engines already account for a substantial share of website discovery. Without readable signals, they cite your competitors — silently.

Unconfigured robots

AI crawlers are often blocked by default, even unintentionally. Your content exists, but engines have never accessed it.

Content that cannot be cited

Structure, sources and clarity: without strong signals, AI prefers a better-prepared competitor, even one with less expertise.

Missing measurement

Without properly configured GTM and GA4, you cannot tell whether fixes pay off. Traffic you cannot see is traffic you cannot defend.

New — Console Ops

The complete loop: measure, decide, publish

The new Ops section closes the loop between measurement and action: track buyer prompts, see when AI cites you — or a competitor — then prepare and publish reviewed content, with evidence at every step.

Tracking

Tracked prompt pool

Up to 200 prompts your customers actually ask ChatGPT and Gemini. Each scheduled check measures mentions, citations and sentiment.

Your API keys stay on the server — never returned to the browser.

Measurement

Live OpenAI / Gemini collections

Bounded runs (5 prompts per batch, 2 batches per run) feed the existing Competition workflow: every mention is a proposal to verify.

Automatic mentions remain provisional until reviewed.

Human review

Confirm or reject each mention

Detection uses heuristics; you decide. Share of voice, trends and lost mentions count only what you have validated.

The product's safeguard against hallucinations.

Rankings

Tracked keywords + AI Overviews

Google position history for your chosen keywords, AI-Overview detection and citations of your domain, with drop alerts (≥ 3 positions, critical at ≥ 10).

Configurable SERP provider, your keys.

Production

Article pipeline with quality gates

Deterministic brief (intent, angles, FAQ) → structured draft. Seven mandatory gates: title, metadata, answer-first, FAQ, length, lists and entities. If a gate fails, publication is blocked.

Optional self-hosted Ollama — no commercial LLM required.

Publishing

WordPress drafts + IndexNow

The draft is sent to WordPress with draft status, after your explicit approval. An optional IndexNow notification can follow.

Never automatically published live. Never.

What the loop will never do: publish without approval, invent a number, query an AI engine without your keys, or claim an engine cites you without measured evidence. Per-client scheduler, disabled by default.

The console

All your data. Your priorities. A clear direction.

Search Console, GA4, GEO, Competition and Ops: one multi-client console, isolated by client, with each tab connected to your real data.

Illustrative interface: a stylised overview. The real console also includes GA4, Bing, AI competition and the Ops loop — with secure Keycloak sign-in.

Roadmap

Three phases, seven workstreams, one requirement: evidence

The planned roadmap extends the audit to what is still missing: measuring what crawlers actually see, your brand beyond the website and content trust — then a single score and the agency workflow.

Phase A — Truth

Measure what exists

Close the audit's blind spots.

  • ●SSR/JS rendering check — compare raw HTML with the rendered DOM: a client-only site is a blocker, not a score.
  • ●Off-site brand scanner — Wikipedia, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub… with evidence per platform and domain-based disambiguation.
  • ●E-E-A-T evaluator — Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness: 4×25 points, deterministic heuristics and excerpts as evidence.

Deliverable: an audit that can no longer score an invisible site.

Phase B — Action

A plan that fits your business

From diagnosis to coaching.

  • ●Block-level citability coach — each passage scored on 5 dimensions; below 60, a rewriting pattern is supplied.
  • ●Business profiles — SaaS, local, ecommerce, publisher: adapted templates, priorities and engine emphasis, instead of a generic plan.
  • ●Composite score v2 — one deterministic, versioned 0–100 score, with the 3 actions that can change it.

Deliverable: the report becomes a task list for each business profile.

Phase C — Business

Agency, from audit to renewal

The workflow that supports a practice.

  • ●Client pipeline — lead → qualified → active, notes, contract value and committed MRR.
  • ●Automatically generated proposals — from the latest audit: summary, scores, 3 service levels, calculated ROI and a 6-month timeline.
  • ●White-label monthly changes — ▲/▼ by category, completed quick wins and a 6-month trajectory in your branding.

Deliverable: the report that supports the next month's engagement.

Full specifications (FS-1 → FS-7), acceptance criteria and PR breakdown: GitHub repository, file GTM-GROWTH-CHANGE-IMPLEMENTATION.md.

Measurement

GTM, measured end to end

Traffic you cannot see is traffic you cannot defend. The same server audits the content that produces the numbers.

Install

Page checks

Loader in the head, noscript, dataLayer order and consent — plus a snippet generator that rejects malformed IDs.

Inspect

Tags, triggers, variables

GA4 configuration and events, duplicate tags and reverse lookups: which trigger fires which tag, which variable is used by which tag.

Prove

Evidence from GA4

Cross-reference GTM events with those actually received in GA4 and validate ecommerce payloads against the official schema.

FAQ

The questions that decide the engagement

Is the free read a real audit ?

Two layers. The URL score runs in your browser: HTTPS, hostname shape, path depth, tracking parameters, fragments, length and extensions — this part fetches nothing. The SEO, GA4 and Search Console tables are measured server-side by /api/free-read, on the page, its robots.txt and sitemap. Without a connected API, these tables are labelled sample ; npm run cli -- geo-free-read --url … returns the same rows locally.

What is GEO, and how does it differ from SEO ?

SEO optimises for a list of traditional links. GEO optimises for being cited in an answer : an engine must retrieve the page, parse it, resolve the entity and find a passage worth citing. They overlap (crawler access, structure, metadata), but a page can rank well and remain hard to cite — which is why citability is scored separately.

How long before AI engines cite me ?

Nobody can promise a date, and any tool that does is guessing. What can be measured: whether crawlers are allowed, whether the entity resolves, whether a passage is citable and how quickly a change is announced (IndexNow). The report provides these, plus the projected score once fixes are delivered.

Does the Ops loop query ChatGPT or Gemini without me ?

No, by design. Live collections use your API keys, configured per client, stored on the server and never returned to the browser. Each run is bounded (5 prompts per batch, 2 batches), creates a dataset to review, and the scheduler is disabled by default. Detected mentions remain provisional until you confirm or reject them.

Can the article pipeline publish by itself ?

No. Seven quality gates block publication while they fail (title, metadata, answer-first, FAQ, length, lists, entities), and even after they pass, sending requires explicit approval. Content is sent to WordPress as a draft — never live without human review. That is the difference between a copilot and autopilot.

Do you need access to my Google account ?

Only for GA4 and Tag Manager audits. They use a service account invited with read access to your properties. Every write — tags, sitemaps, Indexing API and Measurement Protocol secrets — is disabled by default and requires an additional flag plus confirm=true.

What happens after I submit the form ?

You receive the full audit of the submitted URL, the three fixes with the most recoverable points and a short list of measurement gaps that would make the numbers unreliable. If now is not the right time, the audit is still yours.

Is it really open source ?

Yes — Apache-2.0. The GEO rubric is adapted from the MIT-licensed geo-optimizer-skill model, credited in the documentation. The server, CLI, website and tests are in the same repository.

Built on an MIT toolkit. GeoSuite publishes a dependency-free GEO toolkit under MIT; two checks previously missing here are now native (poppy.json and a crawl-based sitemap generator), ported from TryGeoSuite/geo-toolkit and poppy-json — Matteo Perino and GeoSuite. The checks are theirs; the implementation runs here in the same server as the rest of the audit.
